# CANDIDATE: VIX_TERM_CONTANGO_ORB_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

A steep VIX term structure (contango, VIX/VIX1D > 1.3) indicates elevated near-term volatility expectations relative to longer-dated vol, signaling impending mean-reversion. This regime increases the probability that an opening-range breakout will sustain follow-through rather than reverse, as vol contraction supports directional moves. The strategy combines ORB breakout timing with VIX term structure filtering to capture higher-fidelity breakouts.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** At the close of a 5-minute bar that: (1) clears the opening-range high (ORH) with a close above ORH, (2) shows volume ≥ 1.5× the average 5-minute volume of the first 30 minutes, and (3) has VIX/VIX1D ratio > 1.3. Enter long at the bar's close.  
**Exit:** Initial stop at the opening-range low (ORL). Profit target set at 2× the opening-range width (ORH-ORL) above the breakout entry level. Runner portion can be trailed using a 15% ATR-based chandelier exit (using ATR(14) on 5-minute bars) to capture extended moves while protecting gains.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** Strategy trades 0DTE calls (long bias). Full position sizing per Gamma playbook requires $25K+ account for 15 contracts at $1.00 entry premium. $1K paper account would realize ~14% of headline P&L due to position sizing constraints (min 3 contracts).
2. **Sample bias:** No historical sample used; idea derived from vol-regime thesis. High overfit risk until Stage-1 backtest validates edge across regimes.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward or held-out window tested).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (top 3 J days not evaluated for realistic slippage/fill rates).
5. **Failure modes:** 
   - Worst day: False breakout during VIX > 25 (vol spike) triggering stop at ORL, risking 100% of premised premium.
   - Max drawdown: Unknown without backtest; chain of losing days in choppy/low-vol regimes could exceed 50% account drawdown.
   - Blow-up scenario: Persistent backwardation (VIX/VIX1D < 0.9) combined with intraday mean-reversion causing repeated failed breakouts and stops.
6. **Concentration:** Unknown until Stage-1 backtest; if top 5 days exceed 100% of P&L, strategy lacks robustness.
